Corporate NPLs: Driven by TDR strategy and active debt 
management
Corporate NPL balances declined in 2025, reflecting the 
company’s effectiveness in converting assets into cash through a 
disciplined and systematic debt management approach. 
Recoveries were achieved through a combination of debt 
restructuring negotiations and accelerated legal enforcement , 
including cash receipts from both full and partial settlements, as 
well as proceeds collected via LED.
This represents a cash -backed reduction , directly strengthening 
the company’s liquidity position . It also illustrates the natural 
operating cycle of AMC: invest → manage → resolve → collect → 
reinvest, which underpins the company’s ability to generate 
sustainable earnings in subsequent periods.(Unit : Million Baht)

Corporate -Driven Recovery
2025 cash collections remained at a relatively high level, 
although lower than the prior year due to reduced NPA sales 
and the absence of income from NPL servicing activities. 
Nevertheless, the quality of cash inflows improved 
significantly, driven by the successful closure of large -ticket 
deals and the acceleration of legal enforcement processes 
initiated in prior periods.
Corporate NPLs served as the primary contributor, supported 
by both a stable recurring recovery base and sizable lump -sum 
collections from account closures and legal case resolutions 
during mid -year. 
Meanwhile, Housing NPAs continued to enhance the 
consistency of cash flows , helping to reduce overall volatility. 
Together, these elements reflect a revenue structure that 
combines steady recurring inflows with the potential for 
upside from large -ticket resolutions in future periods.(Unit : Million Baht)
